# Where to Watch Faith of Our Fathers


by Angel | September 15, 2026


During the Vietnam War, two young fathers head into battle from very different places. One is a man of deep faith. The other is a cynical doubter. Neither knows how profoundly their lives will affect the sons they leave behind.


Twenty-five years later, those sons meet as strangers. Armed with their fathers’ handwritten letters from the battlefield, they set out together for the Vietnam Veterans Memorial in Washington, D.C. What begins as a journey to understand their fathers becomes an unforgettable road trip filled with discovery, grief, friendship, and hope.


[Stream Faith of Our Fathers now on Angel.](https://www.angel.com/watch/faith-of-our-fathers)


### **Two Fathers, Two Very Different Paths**


The story begins during one of the most difficult periods in American history.


Two young men report for duty in Vietnam, carrying very different beliefs about life and faith with them. One trusts deeply in God. The other approaches the world with skepticism.


Both become fathers. Both go to war. And both leave behind sons who will grow up knowing far less about their fathers than they wish they did.


The differences between the two men give the story an important contrast, but their shared experience in Vietnam ultimately connects their families in ways neither son could have anticipated.


### **More Than a Road Trip**


At first, the journey is about their fathers. As the two sons spend time together, however, it becomes about them, too.


They begin as strangers connected by little more than the men who came before them. Along the road, their shared search creates an unexpected friendship and gives each of them a new perspective on his own father.


The Vietnam War remains an important part of the story, but *Faith of Our Fathers* is ultimately interested in something that reaches beyond the battlefield: the bond between a father and his son.


One Angel Guild member described the film as a “beautiful story of redemption and hope,” while another called it a “heartfelt movie” and “definitely a journey worth watching.”


### **Remembering Those Who Served**


The Vietnam Veterans Memorial gives the journey a powerful destination.


Known simply as the Wall, the memorial lists the names of the Americans who died or remain missing from the Vietnam War. For the two sons, arriving there means confronting the reality of what their fathers experienced and the sacrifices made by an entire generation.


Their journey offers a personal way into that history.


Rather than viewing the Vietnam era only through battles and dates, the film explores its impact through families—the fathers who served and the children who spent years living with the consequences of their absence.


That personal perspective has resonated with viewers who have their own connections to the Vietnam generation.
